title.en: Things Gather Where They Are Loved: Preface to the Record of Collected Antiquities

edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource (集古錄目序), collated with the Sibu congkan edition of Ouyang Xiu's collected works (Wikisource, 歐陽文忠公文集, 集古錄跋尾序); one misprint (伕 for 夫) is corrected from the latter.
edition.zh: 据维基文库所录《集古录目序》，并与《四部丛刊》本《欧阳文忠公文集》（维基文库“集古录跋尾序”）对校；据后者改正一处误字（“伕”作“夫”）。

basis.en: Written in 1062; the author died in 1072.
basis.zh: 作于 1062 年，作者卒于 1072 年。

note.en: Ouyang Xiu spent many years gathering rubbings of inscriptions on bronze and stone, about a thousand scrolls in all, and his notes on them began Chinese epigraphy as a field of study. This preface gives his reasons: copies by hand lose the truth, so he kept rubbings from the stones themselves, and since every collection is scattered in the end, he made a catalogue to hand on to later scholars. Notice how calmly he answers the man who mocks him: everything gathered disperses, and that is no reason not to gather.
note.zh: 欧阳修用了许多年搜集金石铭刻的拓本，总共约一千卷；他为这些拓本写的跋尾，开创了中国的金石学。这篇序交代了他的理由：辗转传抄会失真，所以他保存直接从石上拓下的本子；而任何收藏最终都会散失，所以他另编目录，“以传后学”。请留意他回答讥笑者时有多么平静：凡是聚集的都会散去，但这不是不去聚集的理由。

excerpt.orig: 以謂傳寫失真，故因其石本，軸而藏之。
excerpt.en: Believing that copies made by hand lose the truth, I kept the rubbings taken from the stones themselves, mounted them on rollers and stored them.
excerpt.zh: 以谓传写失真，故因其石本，轴而藏之。

gloss.en: 彊 is the same as 強: the strong, those with power and means.
Passing through more than ten interpreters, that is, through many countries on the way.
gloss.zh: 经过十几道翻译，即途经许多国家。

gloss.en: 𦝫, the waist; 絙, a rope: with ropes tied round their waists.
gloss.zh: 𦝫，同“腰”；絙，粗绳。腰上系着绳子。

gloss.en: 篝火, fire carried in a cage, a lantern; 餱糧, dried provisions.
gloss.zh: 篝火，放在笼中的火，即灯笼；餱粮，干粮。

gloss.en: The bath basin of King Tang of Shang, whose inscription is quoted in the Great Learning: 'If you can renew yourself one day, renew yourself every day.'
gloss.zh: 商汤的浴盘，《大学》引其铭文：“苟日新，日日新，又日新。”

gloss.en: A bronze tripod of the Kong family whose inscription is quoted in early texts: usually taken to be that of Zheng Kaofu, an ancestor of Confucius (Zuo zhuan), or that of Kong Kui (Book of Rites).
gloss.zh: 孔氏的铜鼎，铭文见于先秦典籍：一般认为指孔子先祖正考父的鼎（见《左传》），也有人认为指孔悝的鼎（见《礼记·祭统》）。

gloss.en: The Stone Drums found near Qishan, carved with poems about hunting; they are among the oldest stone inscriptions in China.
gloss.zh: 岐山之南发现的石鼓，刻有记述田猎的诗，是中国现存最早的石刻文字之一。

gloss.en: The stones the First Emperor of Qin had carved on Mount Tai, Mount Yi near Zou, and Mount Kuaiji, praising his reign.
gloss.zh: 秦始皇在泰山、邹县峄山、会稽山所立的颂德刻石。

gloss.en: Five scripts: the ancient script, the large seal (籀), the small seal, bafen (八分) and clerical script.
gloss.zh: 五种书体：古文、籀文（大篆）、小篆、八分、隶书。

gloss.en: King Mu of Zhou, of the tenth century BCE; the oldest item in the collection was a stone inscription attributed to him.
gloss.zh: 周穆王，公元前十世纪的周王；《集古录》中最古的一件，是传为他所刻的石刻。

gloss.en: 石本, rubbings taken directly from the stones, as against copies made by hand.
gloss.zh: 石本，直接从石刻上拓下的本子，相对于手抄本而言。

gloss.en: Mounted on rollers as hand scrolls and stored.
The separate catalogue was eventually compiled in ten volumes by his son Ouyang Fei in 1069.
gloss.zh: 这部目录后来由他的儿子欧阳棐于 1069 年编成十卷。

gloss.en: Ouyang Xiu's colophons on the rubbings often use inscriptions to correct dates, names and offices in the standard histories.
gloss.zh: 欧阳修为拓本写的跋尾，常用碑文订正史书中的年代、人名和官职。

gloss.en: Taking such trouble over something small.
To exchange this, the inscriptions, for that, the ivory, gold and jade others hoard.
gloss.zh: 拿这个（金石拓本）去换那个（象犀金玉）。

note.en: A founding preface of Chinese epigraphy, calm and persuasive on why to gather what will scatter anyway; fine prose, a little formal beside Li Qingzhao’s afterword on the same theme.
note.zh: 中国金石学的奠基序文，从容地讲为何收集终将散失之物；文字精好，与李清照同题的后序相比稍显端正。
